Most Airports Cap Concession Prices… But The System Is A Total Joke

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1167 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Onemileatatime

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Travelers are conditioned to expect high prices at airport retailers and restaurants, so over $5 for a bottle of water at an airport shop, or $25 for a burger at a mediocre airport restaurant, might not catch anyone off guard.
  • Industry observers note that however, did you know there are caps on how much retailers at airports are supposed to be able to charge, and they’re largely just not enforced?
  • Airports generate revenue in a variety of ways, and one of the major ways is through the retailers they have in the terminal.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Travelers are conditioned to expect high prices at airport retailers and restaurants, so over $5 for a bottle of water at an airport shop, or $25 for a burger at a mediocre airport restaurant, might not catch anyone off guard.

Industry observers note that however, did you know there are caps on how much retailers at airports are supposed to be able to charge, and they’re largely just not enforced? Well, or perhaps more accurately, they are enforced, but using very dishonest math. The backstory of this is interesting.

Airports generate revenue in a variety of ways, and one of the major ways is through the retailers they have in the terminal. An airport is like a shopping mall with a very captive audience, and as you’d expect, rent for businesses in airports is absolutely through the roof, as a result of that.

But in order to balance things out and prevent retailers from exploiting consumers, over 80% of airports in the United States specifically stipulate the maximum prices that airports can charge consumers. These terms are typically baked into the contracts that airport retailers sign, and failure to adhere to the rules can lead to consequences, at least in theory.

The airports with pricing caps for airport businesses generally fall into one of two categories:.

It has been revealed that if there are supposed to be rules in place capping airport pricing, then why is this such a widespread concern? More Perfect Union recently published a great video investigating this issue, and it’s a fascinating watch. First they actually analyze airport pricing, and then they confront airport authorities about the lack of enforcement.

Here’s what’s interesting — airport retailers do have to submit comparisons for benchmark pricing, to prove that they’re not violating rules and exploiting customers. The concern is what kind of businesses are considered comparable for the purposes of “street pricing.”.

For example, 9NEWS recently investigated this at Denver Airport, finding that a basic Starbucks coffee cost $4.55 in the airport, compared to $2.95 outside the airport (a 54% markup), and a bag of cashews cost $9.99 in the airport, compared to $4.74 outside the airport (a 110% markup).

The airport’s VP of Concessions agreed to sit down with the reporter to discuss this, and she said the results of his investigation were great news — she suggested that 93% of the prices were compliant, and said “that’s pretty darn good.” How could that be, given the high markups compared to nearby businesses?

The issue boils down to how much latitude businesses have to submit pricing comparisons:.

What’s wild is how the airport official responds to Starbucks just having consistent pricing, and violating the rules:.

VP of Concessions: “What I get from that is, they’re looking for consistency, across the board, across the nation, across the world.”Reporter: “I can’t help but think that travelers may be looking for consistency, but if they see a cheaper cup of coffee, they’ll probably be okay with it.”VP of Concessions: “I don’t know the answer to that. This is how we take care of our passengers, by ensuring that they are paying fair and transparent pricing, while supporting our business partners.”.

Back to the original story, the More Perfect Union reporter confronted the Port Authority of Latest York and New Jersey about pricing like $6.89 for one liter of Smart Water, compared to closer to $3.50 at nearby bodegas.

The response was that “comparing a Hudson to a bodega isn’t appropriate,” because “Hudson is a specialty market.” The approved price comparison was reportedly based on the price of water at Tablet Works, a “wellness & concierge pharmacy” in a high-end mall.

The other thing to keep in mind is that a large percentage of airport retailers and restaurants are run by the same few companies, like HMSHost, which is a subsidiary of Avolta. So clearly they have a centralized approach to submitting pricing comparisons, and know exactly what they’re doing. Interestingly, the few independent businesses in some airports were found to have the most honest pricing.

So to sum it up, the system is designed to be rigged. Airport authorities can technically pretend they’re looking out for consumers by setting a cap. Retailers can submit pricing comparisons to the highest prices they can find anywhere. Then airport authorities verify those prices to pretend they’re doing their jobs.

Airports are obviously complicit in all of this. They make money by charging sky high rent, and the reason they can do that is because retailers can charge hugely inflated prices. The more profits retailers make, the more airports can charge in rent. And they know that no consumer is going to avoid an airport because of high concession costs.

Around 80% of airports in the United States cap the prices that retailers can charge, so in most cases, you’re not supposed to be paying more than 15% above “street pricing.” The issue is the liberties that businesses can take with what constitutes “street pricing.”.

In a recent development, the price of the bottle of water or smoothie you’re buying isn’t compared to what you’d pay at a nearby gas station and smoothie shop, but instead, is being compared to what you’d pay at Erewhon. Talk about a very broken system, with no incentives for any party to actually be honest….

What do you make of this airport pricing situation?

  • Flynn, the author of The Man Who Invented Conservatism: The Unlikely Life of Frank S.

Recent findings suggest that the British first edition of The Managerial Revolution that I picked up in a Charing Cross Road shop a quarter century ago tells us much about the work itself. I’ve read it four times, conscripted it as an airplane companion, and brought it to the beach. Yet its binding remains strong, its cover quite flexible, and its pages yellowing but intact. We no longer much refer to let alone read such 1941 bestsellers as Clifton Fadiman’s Reading I’ve Liked or Margaret Leech’s Reveille in Washington. But James Burnham, much like my strong and solid copy of his most famous book, endures.

Industry observers note that burnham, who entered the world 121 years ago Sunday and left it nearly 40 years ago, very much remains part of the Great Conversation. The Managerial Revolution, anticipating as it did the ascension of technocrats, specialists, and the bureaucratic elite as a sort of ruling class, surely helped in that regard. Burnham remains read, despite no Burnhamite clique in academia or organized faction among movement conservatives dedicated to advancing his ideas. Kirkians, Straussians, and Randians exist. Why no James Burnham Preservation Society with an accompanying secret handshake?

Daniel J. Flynn, the author of The Man Who Invented Conservatism: The Unlikely Life of Frank S. Meyer, is an American Spectator senior editor, visiting fellow at the Hoover Institution, and YouTuber @RightWingWilderness.

On “The Complex Reputation of James Burnham”.

#54074. Why Are All Pratt & Whitney's GTF Engines Green On The Inside?

📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1624 w)
📖 Baca

Why Are All Pratt & Whitney's GTF Engines Green On The Inside?

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1624 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Simpleflying

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that passengers boarding an Airbus A320neo or an A220 who glance at the engine intake from the jet bridge often notice something unusual.
  • Industry observers note that the more convincing answers sit in materials science and maintenance practice.
  • The broad green band lining the inner surface of the fan case is the engine’s acoustic liner, a panel built from a perforated skin bonded over a honeycomb core.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that passengers boarding an Airbus A320neo or an A220 who glance at the engine intake from the jet bridge often notice something unusual. Inside the nacelle, ahead of the fan blades, a ring of teal green lines the casing of the Pratt & Whitney Geared Turbofan, whether the aircraft carries the PW1100G of the A320neo family or the PW1500G of the A220. The color is consistent enough across the fleet that spotters and online aviation communities have debated its purpose for years, with explanations ranging from branding to corrosion protection.

Industry observers note that the more convincing answers sit in materials science and maintenance practice. Two separate components contribute to the green appearance, each with its own function and its own reason for the shade it carries, and a third factor, the practical needs of the people who inspect the engines, explains why the color has persisted. Examining those components in turn clarifies how a modern geared turbofan manages noise, tip clearance, and inspection, and why a seemingly cosmetic detail reflects engineering decisions made well before the engine reaches an airline.

The broad green band lining the inner surface of the fan case is the engine’s acoustic liner, a panel built from a perforated skin bonded over a honeycomb core. The perforations admit sound waves into the cells of the honeycomb, where each cell behaves like a small resonant chamber that absorbs acoustic energy and converts a portion of it into heat. By sizing the cells and the perforated face sheet for particular frequencies, designers tune the panel to dampen the tones that dominate fan noise.

The geared architecture makes this component especially relevant. Because a reduction gearbox lets the fan turn more slowly than the turbine driving it, the engine produces a different acoustic signature from a direct-drive fan of similar size, with more of the energy at lower frequencies. Low-frequency sound is harder to absorb than high-frequency sound, since longer wavelengths need deeper cavities to dissipate effectively, which is why the liner occupies a generous stretch of the inlet. Pratt & Whitney has promoted the engine’s reduced noise footprint as a headline benefit, and the liner is one of several features that contribute to it alongside the slower fan itself.

Construction follows a sandwich principle common to aerospace structures. A solid backing sheet closes one side of the honeycomb, and the perforated face sheet closes the other. The arrangement delivers acoustic performance with very little weight, a priority in any component carried on an engine hanging from the wing, where added mass raises fuel burn. The panels are also designed to withstand airflow, vibration, temperature swings, and minor debris impacts throughout a long service life.

It has been revealed that the teal shade is generally attributed to the composite itself rather than to a decorative coating. According to descriptions of the construction, the resin and epoxy matrix that bind the liner’s layers carry a natural pigmentation that indicates through on the finished surface. Engineers have a practical reason to avoid covering it. A thick film of paint would partially fill the microscopic perforations in the face sheet, reducing the open area through which sound enters the cavities and degrading the attenuation the panel was designed to achieve.

However, this explanation should be treated with some caution, because there has not been a published manufacturer statement regarding the color. As a result, the exact origin of the hue remains an informed inference rather than a documented fact. The uniform result across A320neo and A220 installations nonetheless suggests a controlled material choice instead of an incidental one.

Directly aft of the acoustic ring sits a slightly lighter blue-green band, the abradable rub strip, which technical literature also calls a fan outer air seal. Its job is to control the gap between the fan blade tips and the surrounding case. Any air that leaks across that gap represents lost work, so engine makers want the clearance as small as practical without allowing the blades to strike a hard surface.

According to recent reports, the abradable material solves that problem by being softer than the blade tips. During break-in, the tips cut a shallow groove into the strip, producing a seal matched to the actual shape of that particular fan, including any slight growth caused by heat and centrifugal loading. The strip wears while the blades and the case remain intact. A paper from the 2003 NASA Seal/Secondary Air System Workshop, which covers Pratt & Whitney abradable seals, documents the broader engineering approach behind such materials.

It has been revealed that the color of this strip carries its own explanation. The compound is supplied as a two-part epoxy and hardener, and the components are mixed to a defined turquoise shade so that a uniform color confirms the two parts were blended properly before application. Streaks or patches of a different tone would signal incomplete mixing, and with it a risk that the cured strip will not abrade predictably. The compound’s behavior over time matters as much as its initial performance. As the engine accumulates cycles, the strip gradually erodes from airflow, particles, and repeated light contact, and clearance grows accordingly. Operators therefore monitor the condition of the strip during scheduled inspections and restore it when wear exceeds published limits, a process that depends on repeating the same mixing and curing steps, and the same color check, each time the material is applied.

Beyond material chemistry, the saturated green interior gives maintenance crews a practical advantage during walk-around checks. The fan case sits in a shadowed cavity, and the blades, the hub, and any dark residue around the casing can blend together in poor light. A bright, uniform background makes departures from normal appearance easier to see.

Ramp inspectors look for several conditions in this region. Foreign object debris, such as fragments of tire, packing material, or bird remains, stands out against the green surface. Erosion of the liner or the rub strip indicates as lighter patches or exposed honeycomb, and abnormal wear on the blade tips appears as unusual rub patterns where the strip has been cut. Because these checks often occur between flights under airport lighting and on tight schedules, a background that makes anomalies obvious reduces the chance of a missed finding.

Industry observers note that the choice of green also reflects how the human eye distinguishes color. Green sits near the middle of the visible spectrum, where daylight vision is most sensitive, and it contrasts strongly with the reds, browns, and oranges typical of oil, hydraulic fluid, and corrosion products, so a stain or deposit on the liner is easier to notice than it would be on a gray or white surface.

The GTF is far from the first aircraft component to appear in this color. Aerospace suppliers have long finished parts in green, and BMT Aerospace notes that the shade is often traced to protective primers applied to metal surfaces to resist corrosion. Zinc chromate primer, widely used for decades on airframes and components, has a distinctive yellow-green tone, which is why green surfaces are a familiar sight inside wheel wells, wing bays, and equipment racks.

Industry observers note that public discussion has also linked the GTF’s green interior to Pratt & Whitney’s environmental positioning, since the engine is marketed on lower fuel burn, reduced emissions, and quieter operation. This reading is plausible as a secondary benefit but lacks documentary support, and the engineering explanations above are sufficient on their own. A color that doubles as a reminder of the engine’s efficiency claims costs the manufacturer nothing, which may be why no one has felt a need to change it.

The green interior of the GTF is a small example of a larger trend in which material properties are doing more of the work that markings once did. As engines move toward larger, slower fans housed in shorter nacelles, liners will have to absorb more sound from less surface area, which pushes designers toward more sophisticated core geometries and multilayer constructions. Pratt & Whitney’s improved GTF Advantage variant retains the same gearbox architecture, so the existing liner conventions should carry forward into the newer engines.

Sources indicate that inspection practice is also changing. Airlines and maintenance providers are adopting borescope automation, drone-assisted visual checks, and machine-vision software that compares images against a reference baseline. A controlled, repeatable color simplifies that comparison, because software can flag deviations in hue or texture more reliably when the underlying surface is uniform. Should manufacturers publish color tolerances for liners and rub strips, the green interior could evolve from an informal convention into a formal measurement reference, with deviations scored automatically before a technician reaches the engine.

Material choices will also respond to environmental scrutiny. Chromate-based primers are under regulatory pressure in several jurisdictions because of worker exposure and disposal concerns, and the industry is moving toward alternatives. Any substitute for current coatings will need to preserve acoustic openness, bonding strength, and the visual contrast that crews rely on, which may lead suppliers to add deliberate pigments where natural color once sufficed.

Industry observers note that for the existing fleet, the near-term picture is straightforward. With a large and growing fleet in service, the teal ring is likely to remain a recognizable feature for decades, and its meaning will rest on data as much as on appearance. Operators who record inspection images consistently over an engine’s life will build a visual history of wear that could support condition-based maintenance, replacing fixed intervals with decisions informed by measured trends in clearance and liner condition. In that sense, the color’s greatest value may lie ahead of it, as a standardized backdrop for the analytics that will govern how these engines are maintained.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Emirates is known for being a world-class airline, though at this point, the carrier’s ground experience at Dubai International Airport (DXB) leaves a lot to be desired, especially for premium passengers.

While I don’t want to suggest that the carrier’s first class lounges and business class lounges are terrible, they’re far from cutting edge, and the design definitely feels extremely outdated. Earlier this year, I wrote a post asking if Emirates was going to revamp its lounges at the airport, or just wait until the theoretical move to Dubai World Central (DWC) around 2032.

According to recent reports, well, it seems that my concerns have now been addressed, as Emirates has declared looks to completely transform its lounge experience in Dubai. Over the summer we saw the airline start to roll out a new global lounge concept for outstation lounges, and that idea is now coming to Dubai as well.

In a recent development, as is the case for any airline, rolling out a upcoming lounge concept at a hub airport isn’t easy, given that it requires spaces to be closed. So that’s why it’s worth noting that Emirates is taking an innovative approach to refreshing its lounges in Dubai:.

In a recent development, emirates is investing a total of 400 million AED ($109 million) in these lounge spaces. Interestingly, Emirates claims that “all flagship lounges” will be getting a redesign, though there’s zero mention of the lounges in Concourse A, which are the biggest lounges in the world (they span the entire concourse), and offer direct boarding to planes. So it’s not clear when those lounges will undergo updates.

Here’s how Emirates President Tim Clark describes this development:.

According to recent reports, “Our customers expect the very best from Emirates, whether while flying or spending time with us on the ground. We believe the airport experience should be every bit as exceptional as the journey itself, and that’s why we are transforming our lounges globally. This new First Class Lounge in Dubai is the first taste of what’s to come. And if these are the lengths we will go to for a temporary lounge… just imagine what you can expect from new Emirates Lounges going forward. Over the next two years, we’ll be unveiling a completely different lounge experience, with new concepts in dining, wellness, entertainment and personalised hospitality. We’re going well beyond a traditional refurbishment and creating extraordinary spaces.”.

We’ve already seen how Emirates is overhauling its global lounge network, and I’d say the changes are pretty awesome. So what can we expect in Dubai? As you can see, Clark references how the temporary newly introduced first class lounge is just a small glimpse into what we can expect in the future. Below is a video showing the new concept, and I must say, it looks impressive!

Here’s how Emirates describes the lounge concept, broadly:.

Industry observers note that featuring immersive culinary experiences to dedicated wellness facilities and innovative entertainment concepts, Emirates is redefining what customers can expect from their time at the airport. Building on Emirates’ renowned hospitality, customers can expect distinct spaces for dining, relaxation, work and socialising – complemented by intuitive technology, refined interiors and elevated personal service. Each lounge will bear the hallmarks of the iconic Emirates brand, with the interiors conveying luxury, comfort, exceptional hospitality and global appeal.

When it comes to the temporary newly introduced first class lounge, here are the details:.

As much as people like to suggest that Gulf carriers just throw money down the drain when it comes to passenger experience, Emirates is actually a pretty disciplined and cost focused business, which is also clear based on the fact that the airline still has angled business class seats with seven seats per row. 😉.

But when the airline does invest and upgrade its products, it has a pretty good sense of what customers like. Barista coffee, Dom Perignon, and a gym? Count me in (though maybe the amenities shouldn’t be enjoyed in that order). 😉 It does sound like there still won’t be dedicated bedrooms, which would be disappointing, but also wouldn’t surprise me, given the volume of rooms they’d need to serve guests.

Two things stand out to me here:.

Emirates is hugely investing in its lounge network in Dubai, something that’s long overdue, if you ask me. Over the next two years, at least four lounges will be getting a full makeover, to match the carrier’s latest lounge aesthetic.

Recent findings suggest that we’ve just seen the opening of a new temporarily first class lounge in Concourse B, which is described as an example of what’s to come. Next year that lounge is expected to become a business class lounge, as a new flagship first class lounge opens, along with additional first and business class lounges.

The fresh design aesthetic looks great, and it sounds like some thought is being put into amenities as well. I look forward to seeing this transformation, though I can’t help but wonder if this reflects a delay with Emirates moving to its new hub airport.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that rep. Nydia M. Velázquez, D-N.Y., is the sponsor of a Cuba war powers resolution filed in May. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call).

Progressive advocates are urging House Democrats to force a vote during the lame-duck session on a resolution aimed at preventing war against Cuba, arguing the glitch is too urgent to wait until Democrats control the chamber next year.

“The Cuban people are suffering and dying, and cannot afford further months of inaction,” 50 progressive groups wrote to Democratic House leaders in a letter dated Wednesday. “In the midterm elections, U.S. voters resoundingly rejected a foreign policy of war and domination, and made clear their desire for Congress to act forcefully to rein in the Trump administration.

Holding a vote would demonstrate that Democrats recognize the urgency facing the Cuban people, and would help set the tone for an assertive agenda of peace, diplomacy and respect for international law in the 120th Congress, the letter added.

It has been revealed that at problem is a war powers resolution introduced in May by Rep. Nydia M. Velázquez, D-N.Y., and House Foreign Affairs Committee ranking member Rep. Gregory W. Meeks, D-N.Y., that would call on the president “to remove the United States Armed Forces from hostilities within or against Cuba, unless explicitly authorized by a declaration of war or a specific authorization for use of military force.”.

The letter was sent to House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries of Latest York, Meeks and House Rules Committee ranking member Jim McGovern, D-Mass. It was signed by prominent anti-war groups such as Win Without War, Just Foreign Policy, the Friends Committee on National Legislation, Indivisible and Code Pink.

Advocates are frustrated that House Democrats have not forced a vote on a Cuba war powers resolution even as they have forced multiple war powers votes on Iran and see it as an example of leadership that is at odds with the progressive wing of the party. One advocate who requested anonymity to speak candidly noted it’s their understanding Democratic leaders are hesitant to make potentially vulnerable Florida members of the caucus vote on the issue.

Spokespeople for Jeffries and Meeks did not respond to requests for comment Wednesday on whether Democrats will force a vote before the end of the year, what their reasoning is if they don’t and whether they proposal to bring up a vote next year.

Senate Democrats sought to force a vote on a similar resolution earlier this year, but Republicans in that chamber successfully derailed the effort. Senate Republicans raised a point of order that the resolution was not entitled to privileged status under the War Powers Resolution since U.S. troops aren't actively engaged in combat against Cuba. The point of order was sustained in a mostly party-line vote of 51-47.

Senate Democrats later introduced another Cuba war powers resolution, which they have not tried to force a vote on and have not signaled they will do so before the end of the year.

The resolutions have come amid several veiled threats from President Donald Trump suggesting eventual military action against Cuba.

“I want to get Cuba done before I leave,” Trump told conservative radio host Hugh Hewitt last week when asked if he would order the use of military force against Cuba.

“Frankly, I’d love to be able to do it for the people, for the Cubans that came and were treated really badly, and they came to America,” Trump noted, adding he would “certainly consider” taking military action.

Sources indicate that trump’s comments are on top of a pressure campaign his administration has been waging against Cuba. Since January, the United States has imposed a blockade of oil shipments to the island, causing fuel shortages that have led to lengthy blackouts and aggravated an economic crisis.

While the Senate vote in April did not go Democrats’ way, advocates still saw it as sending a strong message.

“Despite falling short of the majority, this was among the strongest votes in congressional history against the use of blockades, and one of the most important stands Congress has taken against U.S. economic sanctions toward Cuba in over six decades,” the letter from progressive organizations noted. “The House should take a similarly forceful action at this crucial moment.”.

The House vote, even if successful, would be largely symbolic since the measure Democrats can force a vote on is a concurrent resolution. Concurrent resolutions are widely considered to be nonbinding even if cleared by both chambers of Congress since they do not get a presidential signature, though anti-war advocates dispute that applies to war powers.

The progressive groups in their letter called for “decisive leadership” in forcing a vote on the glitch.

“Across the political spectrum,” the letter noted, “Americans do not want another regime change war, nor an open-ended, nation-building project abroad based on false pretenses — especially not when escalation risks exposing the United States to new national security risks, placing US servicemembers in harm’s way, stoking regional instability, and becoming the latest chapter in a long history of harmful U.S. regional policies that have fueled mass migration to U.S. shores.”.

It has been revealed that last Friday we saw the worst disruption to air travel that we’ve seen in the United States in over 25 years, as air traffic shut down nationwide for over four hours. We promptly learned that this happened because L3Harris, a government contractor, was doing maintenance to switch telecommunications lines from copper to fiber.

The logical question is how something going wrong with the work of one contractor could cause our entire aviation ecosystem to shut down:.

So, what’s actually going on here? A fresh report sheds some more light on this….

Sources indicate that CNN has some insights into how little oversight there was of the work being performed by FAA contractor L3Harris, which led to the ground stop disaster that we saw. When was oversight reduced? Well, in early 2025, coinciding with the FAA laying off a large number of employees, as part of Elon Musk’s “Department of Government Efficiency” (DOGE) stunt.

According to recent reports, according to this report, last Friday morning, an FAA technician escorted a contractor from L3Harris into a remote radio communications site for air traffic control in southern Arkansas, to replace a decades-old router. The FAA technician’s belief was that his role was done once the contractor entered the facility, according to people familiar with what happened, plus the union representing FAA employees.

That router replacement ended up being what triggered the communications complications across the country, ultimately leading to the nationwide ground stop.

FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford insists that the L3Harris engineer performing the upgrade “was monitored by an FAA technician” and that a risk assessment was performed, but sources dispute that characterization, pointing out that the technician “was only there to unlock the door,” and that “there was no monitoring.”.

Funny enough, an FAA spokesperson later contradicted Bedford, saying “the FAA escort is responsible for providing the L3Harris technician access to and from the building,” and “because it is L3 equipment, the escort is not there while the technician is doing work.” It’s amazing how they can’t even keep their narrative straight.

Sources indicate that this type of hands-off arrangement is apparently a recent development that happened under the Trump administration, and a change to how the FAA used to handle things. In March 2025, an FAA memo laid out changes to how FAA maintenance and upgrades would be carried out, in order to speed things up. The memo stated that “it is critical to approve maintenance performed by the Telecommunication Vendors without delay.”.

With this policy, the FAA also went from receiving maintenance “requests” from private contractors that needed to be approved, to receiving “notifications” of intended work, noting that “this work will proceed without FAA approval,” if not processed in time.

While the memo claimed that an FAA liaison will evaluate the “purpose, severity, criticality and impact” of the work, there are reportedly only a handful of liaisons nationwide, processing thousands of notifications. In this case, L3Harris reportedly submitted its “notification” with just a few days notice, meaning there was no meaningful oversight.

A spokesperson for the union representing FAA employees explains that “orders were to simply let the contractor in the building,” that he “had no direction to help or assist in any way,” and that “no PASS-represented employee was asked to conduct a risk assessment on this particular upgrade.”.

In a recent development, we’re getting a clearer picture of the circumstances that caused the nationwide ground stop last Friday, the biggest disruption to US air travel since 9/11. A contractor with L3Harris was given access to a site to replace wiring, with virtually no oversight from an FAA employee.

According to recent reports, while the FAA claims that there’s supposed to be oversight of contractor work, in this case the FAA employee was reportedly just tasked with unlocking the door. The approach to overseeing contractor work is reportedly a new system as of March 2025, where contractor work went from being viewed as “requests” to being viewed as “notifications,” with just a handful of people to oversee these requests. 📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Citi Shop takes some of the work out of saving money online.
  • It has broad reach, too, with more than 5,000 participating online merchants.
  • Its ease of use makes it a great resource, but other portals or special discounts may save you more.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Citi Shop takes some of the work out of saving money online. Once you've installed its browser extension, it acts as a shopping portal and coupon hunter all-in-one, rewarding you with statement credits.

It has broad reach, too, with more than 5,000 participating online merchants. That's easier than a traditional online shopping portal, which requires you to remember to start at the portal and click through before filling your cart.

Its ease of use makes it a great resource, but other portals or special discounts may save you more.

Here's how Citi Shop works and what to consider to determine if it's the best savings path for you.

Citi Shop is a free browser extension for primary cardholders with an eligible Citi credit card, including ThankYou points cards and cobranded cards. Citi retail and commercial cards are usually ineligible.

Offers come as either a percentage back or a fixed amount back, and your earnings are applied as a statement credit on the Citi card you selected during enrollment.

Citi Shop is separate from Citi Merchant Offers, which requires you to enroll in targeted offers with a specific Citi card and then use that card for the qualifying purchase.

Both Citi Shop and traditional portals give you an extra reward for making purchases they track.

According to recent reports, but Citi Shop brings potential rebates to you, rather than requiring you to initiate your savings search. The extension automatically displays a pop-up with an available offer when you visit a participating website. You'll have the option to activate the offer before checkout.

All of Citi Shop's rebates are provided as statement credits, unlike the potential airline miles, hotel points or credit card rewards of traditional portals.

Recent findings suggest that what I like about Citi Shop is that it also acts like a shopping assistant. Instead of opening six coupon sites only to discover that every code expired last Tuesday, it handles the scavenger hunt for you and tests available promo codes on your behalf.

Like Capital One Shopping, Citi Shop uses a browser extension. However, Capital One Shopping doesn't require a Capital One card to enroll and its rewards can be redeemed for eligible gift cards instead of a statement credit.

Generally speaking, Citi Shop clashes with other shopping portals. Both work by referring and tracking your purchase, so they can be mutually exclusive. You'll need to make your purchase through whichever offer is better.

Related: Chase shopping portal guide: How to earn bonus Ultimate Rewards points.

Recent findings suggest that unless Citi Shop finds a promo code, it won't lower your total at checkout. Its returns arrive later as statement credits and may require patiently waiting two to six months, sometimes longer.

Even though you need an eligible Citi card to enroll, you don’t have to pay with it. Citi allows any payment method accepted by the merchant.

In a recent development, I really appreciate the flexibility to choose the best card for each purchase. For electronics, I might pick a card with an extended warranty while I might stick to a travel rewards credit card for hotel bookings. You can even pay with a gift card if you wish.

Regardless of how you pay, the statement credit will post to the Citi card you enrolled.

Sources indicate that if you have an eligible Citi card but rarely remember to click through a shopping portal, Citi Shop is an easy win. Install it, activate offers when the pop-up appears and let the credits come to you. That convenience can also be a significant benefit if you have partners or other family members who aren't as motivated to strategize on rewards as you are.

Sources indicate that but with a little extra effort, you might be able to earn even more. When the Citi Shop pop-up appears with an offer, take a minute to compare before you click Activate.

Checking a shopping portal aggregator such as Cashback Monitor shows payouts from multiple cash-back, airline and credit card portals, making it easier to compare a Citi Shop statement credit with points or miles elsewhere.

Recent findings suggest that suppose a $200 jacket is marked down to $160. Citi Shop finds a $10 coupon, bringing the checkout price to $150, and offers 8% back. Assuming the full amount qualifies, you'd receive a $12 Citi Shop credit. If you pay with a card that earns 2% back and has an activated merchant offer for $5 off a $100 purchase, you'd collect another $8. After all the credits and rewards post, your net cost would be $130.

Industry observers note that read the terms before getting too excited. Some brands, products, gift cards or coupon codes may be excluded and you might not be able to stack every layer every time. Still, you can often use multiple discounts simultaneously for a better deal.

Citi Shop is not a program for instant gratification. Citi says statement credits post 61 to 180 days after a completed purchase, though some can take longer.

Industry observers note that in many cases, offers may show as pending long before they officially pay out, to account for potential returns. Hotel rewards may remain pending until after the stay. Eventually, you'll see it on your statement as "CITI SHOP STATEMENT CREDIT.".

If a credit hasn't posted after the expected window, contact Citi using the number on the back of your enrolled card. You may want to keep good records along the way, like a screenshot of the offer and an e-receipt from the purchase.

Citi Shop's biggest advantage is convenience. It does the heavy lifting by reminding you to activate offers so you don't miss out on earnings from your online orders, while testing coupon codes along the way. The offers themselves may or may not be the highest available, but they are certainly the easiest.

To truly optimize your returns, you'll want to compare Citi Shop earnings with those from other shopping portals — and stack other forms of saving along the way. But when that sounds like too much, the ease of this extension can still be a great way to tack on some extra returns.

#54066. The American Genius of Madden

The American Genius of Madden

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (876 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nationalreview

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Russell’s Madden, as its story of the Oakland Raiders football coach John Madden shifts between semidocumentary and biopic.
  • According to recent reports, the key to the film’s geniality and surprise is Nicolas Cage’s astounding portrayal of Madden, a former college athlete who blew out his knee but kept his feeling for football.
  • Industry observers note that madden became coach for the Raiders, a team known to play with sheer guts and dedication — qualities the burly Buddha shared with team owner Al Davis (Christian Bale), his wiry, sharklike best friend.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Hang on at the start of David O. Russell’s Madden, as its story of the Oakland Raiders football coach John Madden shifts between semidocumentary and biopic. Russell’s uneven, sketchy narrative steadily turns into a probing human comedy. It’s also a slyly monumental tale of American genius found in an Everyman’s commonplace ambition.

According to recent reports, the key to the film’s geniality and surprise is Nicolas Cage’s astounding portrayal of Madden, a former college athlete who blew out his knee but kept his feeling for football. Cage enters the mindset of a sports fanatic who is also an artist, devising plays and strategies that, considering his size and vision, earn him the nickname “Buddha.” But this is not one of those freak-outs that Cage is known for; he seems to transform himself into John Candy — broad-beamed with a tuft of blond hair and a convincing smile. Cage commits to this genial eccentric who, despite his unreachable idiosyncrasy, is harmless, lovable yet tough — an authentic, original American.

Industry observers note that madden became coach for the Raiders, a team known to play with sheer guts and dedication — qualities the burly Buddha shared with team owner Al Davis (Christian Bale), his wiry, sharklike best friend. This thick-and-thin Laurel-and-Hardy pair sustain an unlikely partnership. It’s one of the most remarkable depictions of brotherhood in movies — a friendship that persists over temperamental tensions, even after Madden leaves the team and pursues media entrepreneurship to sustain his love of the sport. Madden the broadcaster converts his playbook ingenuity and follows his father’s advice: “Get away with doing what you love for as long as you possibly can.”.

It has been revealed that russell redeems himself with the oddest-yet-normal collection of American eccentrics. Acting on the edge of parody, Cage and Bale, with their uncanny sincerity, reward Russell’s interest in quirkiness. (Madden hears Davis’s voice in his head.) The fascinating scoundrels of Russell’s terrific American Hustle were preoccupied with manipulating one another. Here, friendship, comradeship, teamwork, and family complications are genuinely recognizable. Scenes that emulate a documentary approach — Madden’s wife Virginia (gung ho comedienne Kathryn Hahn) rivals Jennifer Lawrence’s volatility when speaking directly to the camera — satirize realism to fulfill the non-cynical view of national character that Russell fumbled in the bohemian sojourn of Amsterdam. No wonder De Niro is left out of this particular silver-lined playbook.

Nicolas Cage (John Madden) in Madden.

Chuck Zlotnick/Amazon MGM Studios.

In a recent development, the patchwork of styles in Madden suggests that Russell investigates American eccentricity as he goes along, finding his way back to the coast-to-coast realness that made his Flirting with Disaster so exhilarating (as in Madden’s surreal, unapologetic pitch for the unique holiday dish the Turducken). Russell adopts Madden’s football-analysis style, such as on-screen telestrator vectors, to humorously examine Madden’s own career shifts and twists of personality (Madden instructing his players, or meeting colleagues Pat Summerall, Howard Cosell, and Bob Costas).

Industry observers note that A dull-witted filmmaker, say James Cameron, would choose an “immersive” style for a movie concerned with the gestalt of football. But Russell’s film is also about the phenomenon of a sport that becomes a vanguard of technology and culture. Madden is pursued by Trip Hawkins (John Mulaney), founder of video game manufacturer EA (Electronic Arts), who wants to translate Madden’s football theories for a newly introduced generation of at-home fans and gamers. Hawkins’s proposal is scored to Beethoven’s Ninth — another example of Russell’s wit, matching the film’s eclectic score from Barry White and Talking Heads to N.W.A. (“You don’t want to know what that means,” Davis states to Madden.).

Through Madden and Hawkins’s acumen, Russell treats the discovery of a newly introduced world as an aftereffect of folk intelligence and ingenuity. Genius is kidded when Hawkins’s team of four-eyed computer nerds demonstrate jock potential after applying Madden’s plays to their algorithms. It’s a sweet way of conveying the phenomenon that would turn EA’s Madden NFL video game franchise into a $4 billion enterprise (some estimates raise that into double digits), with annual compensation going to the Madden family estate.

More important, Russell (who co-wrote the script with Cambron Clark) sees Madden as a visionary who proudly summarizes TV sportscasting as “They state the obvious, which is f***ing boring.” My only complaint is that Robert Richardson’s photography tends toward frowzy (perhaps deliberately aping TV docs), not as splendid as Oliver Stone’s Any Given Sunday — the greatest football movie ever made.

Madden itself shares biopic sensibility with John Ford’s The Wings of Eagles, respectfully eschewing its subject’s mortality for an optimistic appreciation of a man’s potential. It is unique to American character and the experience of competition and dreams of the NFL Hall of Fame that Madden shared with Al Davis. Russell’s tribute comes complete with a motto: “You make people feel good and alive and good to be American, and I’m not standing in the way of that.” Thus Russell proves his own resilience and the achievement of a upcoming folkloric genre struggling to emerge.

Armond White is National Review’s culture critic and the author of New Position: The Prince Chronicles and Make Spielberg Great Again: The Steven Spielberg Chronicles.

On “The American Genius of Madden”.

Industry News: Why Virgin Atlantic Is Targeting The 40 RAF Pilots Keeping Britain's F-35 Fleet Flyable

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1499 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Simpleflying

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that the United Kingdom only has around four dozen trained F-35B fighter jet pilots and around 150 Eurofighter Typhoon fighter jet pilots.
  • As the Royal Air Force is so much smaller than the United States Air Force (and Marines/Navy), it lacks depth in pilots.
  • With that being mentioned, airlines will typically focus more on military transport pilots, such as those flying A330 MRTTs and A400Ms.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that the United Kingdom only has around four dozen trained F-35B fighter jet pilots and around 150 Eurofighter Typhoon fighter jet pilots. Losing even a handful of these hard-to-replace pilots to commercial airlines is painful. They are targeted by British airlines, with Virgin Atlantic directly targeting them in its recruitment ads in 2024.

As the Royal Air Force is so much smaller than the United States Air Force (and Marines/Navy), it lacks depth in pilots. Training an F-35 fighter jet pilot can cost around $10 million, and fresh pilots graduating annually in the UK are often measured in the single digits.

With that being mentioned, airlines will typically focus more on military transport pilots, such as those flying A330 MRTTs and A400Ms. Let's examine how Virgin Atlantic seeks to attract ex-RAF pilots and why this is a major problem for the Royal Air Force (and Royal Navy).

In 2024, the publication London Loves Business wrote that "RAF pilots who have operated on F-35 B Lightning II and Typhoon FGR4 are being offered double their annual salary to join Virgin." It adds that those pilots would be given routes to Barbados and New York to quit the RAF and fly with Virgin Atlantic.

It has been revealed that the report stated that the pilots were being offered around double the money that they would typically earn flying for the Royal Air Force. At the time, the Virgin Atlantic advert was reported to read as follows:.

Sources indicate that "In order to be suitable, you must be operating, or have operated in the last three years on one of the following RAF Aircraft: F-35 B Lightning II, Typhoon FGR4. As a member of our Flight Crew, you will be joining the UK’s only exclusively long-haul airline. Flying out of London Heathrow to exciting destinations such as Fresh York, San Francisco, Las Vegas, Delhi, Barbados, Antigua, and many more.".

Recent findings suggest that the advert went on to say that Virgin Atlantic operates the "youngest, cleanest, and most technologically sophisticated" widebody aircraft. Virgin is unusual in exclusively operating a fleet of widebody aircraft. Airlines poaching trained fighter jet pilots is common in many countries, including the United States. For air forces, this can be devastating as it costs around ten million dollars to train a frontline fighter jet pilot and takes years to replace them.

It has been revealed that in a typical Western air force, there should be around 1.3 to 1.5 trained pilots for every fast jet. That said, Britain (and other air forces) have struggled to maintain this figure. While the US military has around 37,000 military pilots, including in the USAF, Army (helicopters), Marines, Navy, and Coast Guard, the British military likely has around 2,500.

Of these, around 1,500 are in the RAF and 500 are each in the Royal Navy and British Army. In 2014, the British Government revealed that there were 1,760 trained regular pilots in the RAF (excluding reserves and other aircrew), although that number has likely declined somewhat over the last decade. However, fighter jet pilots are a small subset of the overall group of pilots.

In late 2022, former Defense Secretary Ben Wallace revealed there were only 30 qualified British F-35 pilots, plus three exchange pilots. By 2023, that number had risen to 34, with seven more soon to graduate. By mid-2026, the RAF had received all of its initially ordered 48 F-38Bs, minus one that fell off an aircraft carrier.

Ideally, the RAF should have around 60–70 or so trained F-35B pilots, but it is unclear how many there are. There have been reports that the ratio may be closer to one pilot per jet, suggesting the RAF may now have somewhere around 45 to 50 trained F-35B pilots. Headlines will often talk about the fighter jets, how many there are, and how ready they are, but pilot availability is often a more pressing bottleneck.

The RAF procured a total of 137 Eurofighter Typhoons. Of these, 26 of the Tranche 1 fighter jets have now been retired, leaving a fleet of four remaining. These are stationed at RAF Mount Pleasant in the Falkland Islands as the UK's farthest air base with a permanent fighter jet presence. They are tasked with defending the islands from Argentina and are supported by A400Ms and A330 MRTTs.

The remaining Typhoons include 67 Tranche 2 and 40 Tranche 3 fighter jets. In January 2026, the British Government stated it would upgrade 40 of them with latest radars and other systems. In July 2026, the budget was significantly increased, and it was reported that all would be upgraded. Britain had previously mentioned the remaining four Tranche 1 fighter jets would retire in 2027, but now it is unclear.

Select aircraft of the Royal Air Force (per RAF).

F-35Bs (shared with Royal Navy).

There has not been an equivalent public disclosure for how many Typhoon fighter jet pilots are serving in the RAF. A reasonable range would be 140-160 trained Typhoon pilots. This would give the RAF a group of up to 200 fast jet pilots in total. Additionally, as of June 2026, the Royal Air Force had 119 trainee fast-jet pilots progressing through the training pipeline, from RAF Cranwell to the point of starting an Operational Conversion Unit.

Beginning around 2015 and then accelerating after COVID-19, the US airline industry has faced an unprecedented pilot shortage. This has affected regional airlines in particular and is made worse by retiring baby boomers. In response, the industry moved to attract former US military helicopter pilots; previously, the focus had been on fixed-wing pilots.

One of the most famous examples was that of Frontier Airlines, which debuted its Rotor Transition Program to help military helicopter pilots transition and receive their fixed-wing qualifications. The program ended up being so successful that, Frontier's website said:.

Sources indicate that "Due to the overwhelmingly positive response and large number of applications we received for our Rotor Transition Program, we have temporarily closed the application window. Keep an eye out for more information regarding the application window opening and future recruitment events.".

Meanwhile, there has not been the same recruitment drive in the UK, as the UK airline industry is much smaller, the military is much smaller (only a few hundred helicopter pilots), and converting is less straightforward. Instead, British industry focuses on recruiting former RAF transport pilots, fast jet pilots, airline cadets, and airline pilots from other airlines.

Sources indicate that in both the United States and the United Kingdom, it is relatively straightforward for fighter jet pilots to transition from flying fixed-wing military aircraft to flying commercial passenger jets. With that being said, the United States has built a considerably more mature and streamlined process.

Recent findings suggest that for ex-British fast-jet pilots, the primary challenge is obtaining the civilian licenses, certifications, and experience required by the UK Civil Aviation Authority. The CAA does recognize military flying experience through its Military Aircrew Accreditation Scheme, meaning that transitioning pilots do not need to start from scratch.

According to recent reports, they can get credits toward their Commercial Pilot License, but still generally need to complete their ATPL theoretical knowledge tests, civilian flight tests, and so on. The entire process of converting from military to commercial jets often takes six to twelve months, depending on how much training credit is granted and the airline course start date.

Industry observers note that in the US, the process typically takes around three to nine months. For comparison, for those starting from scratch in the UK, it typically takes three to over eight years for a pilot to fly with a major airline. It's between two and over six years in the United States, depending on various factors.

According to recent reports, according to Planespotters.net, Virgin Atlantic currently operates an all-widebody fleet of 44 aircraft with an average age of 8.4 years. These include 14 Airbus A330s (six A330-300s and nine A330neos), 12 Airbus A350-1000s, and 17 Boeing 787-9 Dreamliners. This makes it one of the largest all-widebody fleets in the world, although, for comparison, this total would only represent around 15% of Emirates' giant all-widebody fleet.

Virgin Atlantic's outstanding A330-900 orders will replace its remaining fleet of legacy A330-300s by 2027 while growing the overall fleet. The airline was established in 1984 and serves around 29 destinations, mostly from its hubs at London Heathrow and Manchester. The airline is also a member of SkyTeam and is 49% owned by Delta Air Lines. Virgin Atlantic has evolved into a mixed network carrier that serves both leisure-heavy destinations and business-heavy routes.

Industry observers note that it offers flights to Caribbean destinations like Antigua and Barbuda, Barbados, Grenada, Jamaica (Montego Bay), Mexico's Cancun, St. Lucia, and St. Vincent and the Grenadines. Its US destinations include Las Vegas, Orlando, Miami, Tampa, as well as some other less leisure-heavy destinations, such as Boston. Virgin has flights on some other non-leisure routes, including to India and Nigeria.

If Congress ever tries to fix Social Security to address a looming shortfall, a Senate Budget Committee hearing Wednesday demonstrated how poisonous the politics could become.

Budget Chairman Ron Johnson, R-Wis., set the stage for a fierce partisan clash even before the hearing began by calling Social Security a "Ponzi scheme" in a Fox Business interview earlier in the day. Democrats erupted, accusing Johnson of scaring seniors and being unwilling to fix a financial lifeline for more than 72 million retirees.

It has been revealed that “I think it’s outrageous,” stated Sen. Mark Warner, D-Va., one of several Democrats on the panel who slammed Johnson for his comments. “Don’t go out there scaring Americans to make political points on Fox News. This is too fricking key.”.

Johnson acknowledged making an “imprecise comment” on prospects for a fix during the Fox interview. But he also told Democrats that if they had read his “chairman’s memo” he sent them Tuesday they would know he wants to preserve the system and pass a law to prevent any cuts to benefits if the Social Security Trust Fund is depleted.

"This is a scam, it’s grotesque, and at this point there’s really no way to fix Social Security," he noted on Fox Business. "It’s a Ponzi scheme. You can’t fix it. You just shut it down and hope you can recover some of your money.”.

But Johnson appeared to contradict himself later in the same interview, saying there is a difference with a “government-sanctioned Ponzi scheme” in that “you can force investors to keep putting money into it and that’s what we’ll probably have to do … You can fix Social Security and make it solvent.”.

In his opening statement at the hearing, Johnson mentioned Congress should pass a law to prevent benefit cuts and then “roll up our sleeves and begin seriously addressing the main problem, our massive debt and deficits.” He said that is the only way to “ensure we have the financial wherewithal to honor promises made to seniors.”.

Recent findings suggest that johnson also told the panel he used the term “Ponzi scheme” in part to draw attention to the importance of addressing the problem. “If I gotta pay a political price for that, I really don’t care,” he said.

There is no doubt that a fix is needed. Without any change, Social Security recipients face a 22 percent cut in benefits by the end of 2032, according to projections from the Social Security Board of Trustees. Johnson stated Congress and the president won’t cut benefits even if the trust fund is exhausted.

And there has been no shortage of Social Security bills introduced to provide a fix, but none of them has gained momentum.

Recent findings suggest that sen. Bernie Moreno, R-Ohio, drew flak from fellow Republicans after he and Sen. Elizabeth Warren, D-Mass., proposed lifting the cap on income subject to the Social Security payroll tax so that the tax would apply to all earned income.

A bipartisan proposal, from Sens. Richard J. Durbin, D-Ill., Bill Cassidy, R-La., Tim Kaine, D-Va., and John Cornyn, R-Texas, would have put a plan in motion by requiring the Social Security Advisory Board to recommend a bill that would ensure Social Security is funded for at least the next 50 years.

Senators on both sides of the aisle said they were committed to fixing Social Security. Republicans stressed the importance of economic growth to bring in more revenue to the system and cautioned that tax increases would slow growth.

Democrats pitched shifting more revenue into the system, for example by raising the cap on the payroll tax or taxing other income.

“I do believe if we can be focused on fixing the Social Security stability issue, that could be a stepping stone to fixing broader problems,” said Kaine, who is anticipated to chair the Budget Committee when Democrats take over Congress next year.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Washingtonians have a new option to Portugal next summer.
  • In a recent development, TAP Air Portugal will launch a upcoming thrice-weekly service from Dulles International Airport (IAD) to Porto Airport (OPO) on March 30, 2027.
  • It has been revealed that TAP, a Star Alliance partner of United Airlines, will fly an Airbus A321LR on the newly introduced IAD-OPO route.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Washingtonians have a new option to Portugal next summer.

In a recent development, TAP Air Portugal will launch a upcoming thrice-weekly service from Dulles International Airport (IAD) to Porto Airport (OPO) on March 30, 2027. Westbound flights will operate on Wednesdays, Fridays and Saturdays through the summer, and on Mondays, Wednesdays and Fridays beginning in October.

It has been revealed that TAP, a Star Alliance partner of United Airlines, will fly an Airbus A321LR on the newly introduced IAD-OPO route. The long-range, single-aisle aircraft is fitted with 16 lie-flat business-class seats and 155 economy seats.

It has been revealed that the new Portugal route is the latest international addition at IAD. United aims to launch new service to Toulouse, France, in April and to Milan in May, using its new long-range A321XLR on the former route.

International seats from IAD will increase nearly 7% in the first six months of 2027 compared to this year, schedule data from aviation analytics firm Cirium reveals.

IAD is undergoing a massive, $22 billion redevelopment to bring its infrastructure up to modern standards. The first piece — a 14-gate section of the new Concourse E that includes a new, large United Club — opened earlier in November. Future phases include a new international arrivals facility that would support additional long-haul growth.

This content is hosted by Instagram.

And if the redevelopment strategy stays on schedule, IAD could retire its jet-age mobile lounges by the mid-2030s.

TAP’s fresh OPO route complements its existing service to IAD from Lisbon Airport (LIS).

The state-owned Portuguese airline is in the process of being privatized as part of the Lufthansa Group. The German airline conglomerate plans to buy an initial 44.9% stake in TAP, aiming to close the deal by the first quarter of 2028.

Lufthansa Group chief commercial officer Dieter Vranckx said in October that once the TAP deal is done, Lufthansa intends to integrate the Portuguese airline into its transatlantic joint venture with Air Canada and United.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • In a recent development, today is (apparently) International Men’s Day.
  • The crew consisted of 10 people, comprised of two pilots and eight flight attendants.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There’s still quite a gender gap in the airline industry, with a disproportionate number of pilots being male, and a disproportionate number of flight attendants being female. Airlines will sometimes have special celebrations with all-female crews, so here’s an interesting twist on that.

In a recent development, today is (apparently) International Men’s Day. We often see airlines commemorate International Women’s Day, but there aren’t many airlines that celebrate the equivalent for men… well, except Finnair! The airline has today operated its annual flight with an all-male crew. This was the case for Finnair flight AY1331, from Helsinki (HEL) to London (LHR), using an Airbus A350-900.

The crew consisted of 10 people, comprised of two pilots and eight flight attendants. The gate agents were also all men. So, why is this crucial? Finnair highlights how only around 10% of cabin crew at the airline are male, but the company hopes to see that number grow in the future.

I think this is a fun concept, and it would be nice to see a closer to 50/50 gender ratio in both the cockpit and cabin, as it would show that everyone is given a fair chance at such a career.

It has been revealed that I think it’s worth acknowledging that at many airlines, hiring of flight attendants is still primarily or exclusively based on gender. Now, the policies do vary significantly by airline, but perhaps an extreme example is India’s largest airline, IndiGo, which only hires female flight attendants. It’s literally written on the application, that it’s a job for “Female Indian nationals.”.

It’s all so strange, because the airline has this super enthusiastic page about the importance of diversity in the workplace, and claims “all employment decisions are made solely on the basis of merit and qualifications, without regard to a candidate’s gender…” You mean except the single largest portion of your workforce, which is cabin crew?

What’s interesting is that while those gender restrictions exist in the cabin, roughly 18% of the carrier’s pilots are female, which is way above the global average of 7%. That’s obviously a conscious effort, so I guess the idea is that women can become pilots but men can’t become flight attendants.

In fairness, I suspect part of the motivation here is that IndiGo flight attendants share hotel rooms on layovers, and that is a bit more complicated with mixed genders. Then again, it seems easy enough to just try to pair male flight attendants on trips, so it’s hardly a hurdle that can’t be overcome.

It has been revealed that while we’re used to seeing airlines celebrate International Women’s Day, it’s rare to see an airline celebrating International Men’s Day. Finnair has operated an all-male flight today, intended to highlight how only 10% of flight attendants at the airline are male, and the airline wants to change that. While an unconventional initiative nowadays, I think this is still pretty cool.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Dad, here’s a blog post you should pay attention to (and thanks to Steve for flagging this)….

With banks, it’s typically possible to get your account statements by email or mail. There’s no denying that consumer preferences have shifted over the years, and along those lines, Amex has just sent an email to card members, informing them that “we’re making the switch to paperless.” Here’s the main part of the email:.

We’re making the switch to paperless billing statements and account communications, beginning February 2027.

According to recent reports, here’s what happens nextWe want to help you get ready to make the switch too. So, we’ve enrolled your account listed above in the paperless delivery option – but for now, we’ll continue to send you communications about your account in the mail. We’ll also mail your billing statements for the closing dates of November 2026, December 2026, and January 2027.

Recent findings suggest that after that, we’ll send account communications to you by email, and you’ll receive your monthly billing statements electronically. When they’re ready, you’ll be able to view them anytime by logging in to your account online at americanexpress.com or in the American Express App.

Industry observers note that now, that makes it sound like people will be forced to switch to paperless billing, but I don’t believe that’s actually the case? Because further down in the email, it claims this:.

Recent findings suggest that not ready to go paperless? No problem! You can re-enroll in paper billing statements and account communications by going to americanexpress.com/paperlesssettings, selecting “U.S. Mail,” and following the prompts to opt back in.

So it seems like what’s happening here is that Amex will try to force everyone into paperless billing by making it the default, but maybe those who specifically once again state their preferences for paper billing will be able to maintain that communication method?

Suffice it to say that going back 25 years, a vast majority of people got paper statements for their credit cards, while nowadays a vast majority of people get paperless statements, obviously reflecting the shift we’ve seen in how the internet is used.

It’s funny, because I’m sure 99% of OMAAT readers would be confused at the thought of getting paper bills, and would wonder what purpose that serves. But then there are also people like my dad, who rely on paper statements for their credit cards, pay their statement by phone, etc.

So it does sound like people will have the option of opting back into paper billing after being auto-enrolled in paperless billing, so the concept isn’t being eliminated altogether. Still, for my dad, there would likely be quite the learning curve.

In a recent development, then again, up until less than a decade ago he didn’t have a cell phone and insisted he didn’t need one, while now he kind of loves it, for everything from texting, to Googling all kinds of stuff. That’s of course a double-edged sword as well, because he seems to believe that if the Google AI summary states something, it must be true. We’re not talking things like vaccines. Instead, we’re talking things like whether the salmon at Red Lobster is good, etc. Anyway, I digress….

As of February 2027, Amex will be automatically moving those with paper billing to paperless billing. While the message makes it sound like people will be forced to switch to paperless billing, that doesn’t seem to be the case, as Amex is also telling people they can once again enroll in paper billing statements and account communications if they’re “not ready to go paperless.” So Amex just seems to be trying to thin the ranks here of those using this feature.

According to recent reports, americans should expect their federal agencies to be staffed by experts who gather evidence meticulously before proposing regulations disinterestedly. But that’s not what the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) has done when it comes to personalized pricing.

Last month, the FTC ordered nine major companies — Delta Air Lines, Uber, and Instacart among them — “to provide detailed information that will allow the agency to study the use of personal data to set prices and compensation.” The agency, however, seems to have reached its conclusions already, given the contents of both its order and an enforcement policy proposed in August, which appears partial against personalized pricing and the businesses that employ it.

To start, let me provide the context that Aeromexico’s Boeing 787 fleet currently consists of 25 planes, including:.

Aeromexico is planning on fully overhauling the premium cabins on these planes, as was unveiled by the firm’s CEO at this week’s APEX FTE EXPO 2026.

Recent findings suggest that the initiative is for the 787-9s to get all-new cabins, and in the process, the 787-8s will get the old business class seats from the 787-9s. That means the 787-8s will get reverse herringbone seats, which are still competitive, but of course not cutting edge (though still a huge improvement over the pairs of seats currently on the planes).

Sources indicate that the 787-9s will really become the next-generation flagship planes for the airline, though some patience will be required. The expectation is that the first of these Dreamliners will be retrofitted in the next 18 to 24 months (so hopefully by some point in 2028), and then it’ll likely take a couple of years for the fleet to be upgraded.

According to recent reports, we’ll talk more about the newly introduced business class product as such in a bit, but the idea is that the 787-9s will get business class suites, including a front row “business class plus” product. On top of that, the 787-9s will be getting a premium economy cabin for the first time.

The plane will also have up to 70% more premium seats than before. Right now, Aeromexico’s 787-9s have 36 business class seats, while the retrofitted planes will have a total of 61 premium seats, between business class and premium economy. So I suspect the business class cabin won’t actually get that much bigger, but instead, most of that premium addition will come in the form of the new premium economy cabin.

It’s also worth mentioning that Aeromexico is adopting some Delta-style branding, as Delta owns a 20% stake in Aeromexico, and the two airlines have a close partnership.

Aeromexico’s new premium products will be known as Premier One Suites Plus (the “business class plus” product), Premier One Suites (business class), and Premier (premium economy). It seems the 787-8 business class will just be branded as Premier One, given the lack of suites with doors. It seems that what was unveiled earlier this year was the new Recaro R7 Horizon concept, which is the same idea, but with upgraded technology and customization.

According to recent reports, I imagine that we’ll learn more in the coming months, as this was an unusual way to unveil a new product. But this does seem to be officially happening, so it’s something to look forward to… down the road.
